note: Every candidate here is copied from a document this repository already contains. Nothing was discovered by scanning code, nothing was invented, and the classifications are the honest ones rather than the convenient ones: four of the seven are not routine LOW-risk engineering and say so. See docs/company_os_objective_planning.md section 7.

candidates.title: Teach reserved and credential screening to respect negation
candidates.description: screen_reserved() and screen_credentials() match a trigger term anywhere in the objective text. A sentence that says the term does not apply escalates exactly as one that says it does. The sibling defect in the routing classifier was fixed at da4f3ce; these two functions were disclosed and left.
candidates.problem_statement: screen_reserved() and screen_credentials() in company/engineering/intake.py match trigger terms without regard to negation, so a request stating that a reserved action is not involved still returns DecisionRequired.
candidates.expected_value: Fewer false CEO escalations on routine work, and one screening rule rather than two that disagree.
acceptance_criteria: screen_reserved() returns no DecisionRequired for an objective that negates its trigger term, and still returns one when the term is asserted.
screen_credentials() behaves identically to screen_reserved() on the same negated input.
tests/test_company_engineering_execution.py passes, including a new case per screening function covering the negated and the asserted form.
candidates.notes: Risk is MEDIUM rather than LOW deliberately. The current failure is over-escalation, which is fail-safe; a fix that trims it trades a safety margin for accuracy on the path that decides whether the CEO hears about something. That is a judgement above routine engineering.

candidates.title: Disambiguate bare authentication and migration trigger words
candidates.description: Single-word triggers fire on any mention, including a test name or a line of documentation that merely refers to the concept.
candidates.problem_statement: Bare single-word triggers in company/engineering/intake.py escalate a benign test or documentation mention of authentication or migration to specialist routing.
candidates.expected_value: Routine requests that merely mention a sensitive concept reach the cheaper tier instead of the specialist one.
acceptance_criteria: An objective that names a migration only inside a quoted test identifier derives no specialist domain.
An objective that asks for a schema migration still derives the specialist domain it derives today.
tests/test_company_engineering_execution.py passes with a case for each direction.
candidates.notes: MEDIUM for the same reason as the negation candidate: narrowing a trigger narrows an escalation.

candidates.title: Decide the deployment policy the delegation model measures against
candidates.description: approve_deployment appears in action_autonomy and in no grant. A deployment request escalates with nowhere to stop, which is safe and is not a policy.
candidates.problem_statement: The term deploy in company/engineering/intake.py maps to no specialist domain, no reserved action and no routine-eligibility rule, so a deployment request escalates with no seat able to decide it.
candidates.expected_value: A deployment request would reach a stated answer instead of falling off the end of the chain.
acceptance_criteria: company/delegation_policy.yaml states which seat, if any, may approve each of the five deployment kinds.
blocked_by: a CEO policy decision: Company OS has no deployment policy to delegate against, and inventing one in code would be the delegation model widening itself
candidates.notes: Recorded as a candidate so it stops being invisible. It is not engineering work and must not be selected as any.

candidates.title: Give a provider usage event a stable identifier
candidates.description: Two ingestions of one provider response produce rows nothing can tell apart.
candidates.problem_statement: ResourceUsageRecord in ai_platform/usage.py carries no field that is a stable per-event identifier, so a repeated ingestion of one provider response cannot be de-duplicated.
candidates.expected_value: Usage and cost totals would stop double-counting a re-ingested response.
acceptance_criteria: ResourceUsageRecord carries an identifier that is equal for two decodes of one provider response and different for two responses.
blocked_by: a design decision nobody has taken: no existing field is a stable per-event id, so this needs a schema change, and schema or storage migration is outside routine engineering
candidates.notes: Department is ai_platform, not engineering. Under an engineering-only envelope it is out of scope twice over.

candidates.title: Make the runner blocked_attempt path take --repo-dir consistently
candidates.description: One of the four follow-ups the external runner hardening review recorded and did not address.
candidates.problem_statement: The external runner passes --repo-dir to company.engineering receipt only when a repo_dir is supplied, and the acceptance review recorded the blocked_attempt path as inconsistent with its siblings.
candidates.expected_value: One argument convention across the runner's control-plane calls.
acceptance_criteria: tools/engineering_runner/controlplane.py passes --repo-dir on the blocked_attempt path under the same condition as the receipt path.
tests/test_external_engineering_runner.py passes with a case covering the blocked_attempt argument list.
candidates.notes: capsule_id names no capsule that exists: nothing in knowledge/company_os/capsules declares ownership of tools/, and company-engineering-execution lists tools/** under must_not_modify. The eligibility pass rejects this on capsule_owned, which is the correct answer and not a bug in the candidate.

candidates.title: Decide what a work order with zero required_tests means
candidates.description: The second of the four recorded runner follow-ups.
candidates.problem_statement: The external runner hardening review recorded the zero required_tests policy as an open follow-up, so a work order declaring no tests has no stated meaning in the runner.
candidates.expected_value: A work order with no declared tests would get a stated answer instead of an accidental one.
acceptance_criteria: The runner states, and a test pins, whether a work order with zero required_tests is accepted or refused.
blocked_by: a policy decision about what evidence a receipt must carry when the work order declares no tests

candidates.title: Refuse a work order whose acceptance criterion restates the objective
candidates.description: The defect the first live-delegation pilot exposed: intake authorized a broad CEO objective, copied it into the work order, and derived an unfalsifiable criterion.
candidates.problem_statement: assess_request in company/engineering/intake.py returns authorized for an objective that names no subject, deriving the acceptance criterion The stated objective is implemented, which no reviewer or deterministic QA can falsify.
candidates.expected_value: Planning stops being pushed onto the developer session.
acceptance_criteria: assess_request returns planning_required, not authorized, for an objective that names no subject and carries no candidate.
Every objective the existing engineering suites submit is still authorized.
candidates.notes: Completed by the objective-planning capability itself, in the same pass that created this register. Kept here because a register that only holds open work cannot show what closing one looks like.
